definition: A model design where an encoder processes an input sequence into a representation, and a decoder generates an output sequence from that representation.
details: This architecture underlies many sequence-to-sequence tasks like machine translation and summarization; the original transformer paper used this design, though many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants instead.

explainer.lead: Encoder-decoder architecture splits sequence processing into two jobs: building a representation of the input and generating an output from it. This makes it a natural fit for machine translation and summarization, and the original transformer paper used this design.

tiers.eli5: Imagine one person reading a story and making notes, then another person using those notes to tell a shorter version. The reader is the encoder, and the storyteller is the decoder. Together, they turn one sequence into another, such as a sentence in one language into a sentence in a different language.
tiers.practitioner: Use this design when a model must consume an input sequence and generate a related output sequence, as in translation or summarization. The key interface is the representation passed from the encoder to the decoder. Do not assume every transformer-based system has both parts: many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants.
tiers.paperLevel: For input sequence x and output sequence y, the design can be written as h = Encoder(x), followed by y = Decoder(h), where h is the intermediate representation. The original transformer paper used this encoder-decoder design, while many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants instead.

explainer.example: For translation, the encoder processes the English sentence "The cat sits" into a representation. The decoder then generates the French output "Le chat est assis."

usedIn.name: Machine translation
usedIn.detail: The encoder processes a sentence in the source language, and the decoder generates its translation.

usedIn.name: Summarization
usedIn.detail: The encoder processes the input text, and the decoder generates a shorter output sequence.

components.name: Representation: carries information from the encoder to the decoder.
Decoder: generates the output sequence from that representation.

flow: Provide an input sequence to the encoder.
The encoder processes it into an intermediate representation.
Pass that representation to the decoder.
The decoder generates the output sequence.
explainer.origin: The original transformer paper used an encoder-decoder design.
explainer.lineage: Although this design underlies many sequence-to-sequence tasks, many modern LLMs use decoder-only variants instead.
explainer.whyItMatters: Separating input processing from output generation provides a clear structure for sequence-to-sequence tasks. It connects one model design to applications such as translation and summarization.

diagram.caption: The encoder turns an input sequence into a representation, which the decoder uses to generate an output sequence.
